title: KV cache key tiling, hit-rate modeling, and automated safe-apply for TTL policies
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: We currently tune per-prefix TTLs and cache key shapes manually. This ticket builds an automated pipeline that (1) synthesizes a per-tenant/prefix hit-rate forecast from telemetry and synthetic probes, (2) proposes key-tiling adjustments and TTL ladders to improve unit economics for common workloads, and (3) applies config changes via a staged canary safe-apply with automatic rollback triggers. Goal: Reduce hosted token cost by 8-12% on target workloads while keeping 99th-percentile latency regressions <5% and error rate impact zero. Scope: hit-rate model, key-tiling suggestion engine, TTL ladder generator, safe-apply orchestration, rollback criteria, dashboards and runbook. Out of scope: model quantization and kernel-level runtime changes.
acceptance_criteria: Automated hit-rate forecasting job produces stable forecasts for 95% of prefixes with at least 1K requests/day.
Suggestion engine outputs key-tiling and TTL ladder proposals with estimated cost delta and hit-rate impact for each prefix.
Safe-apply flow can execute canary apply to 1% traffic, monitor metrics, and either promote or rollback automatically based on policy.
End-to-end tests (shadow and small-scale canary) exist and pass in CI; relevant GitHub PR and e2e job linked.
Runbook documented: what to do on sustained rollback, how to diagnose hit-drop vs latency regressions, and how to revert in DB-backed config stores.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Telemetry backfill & sampling - build job to aggregate per-prefix QPS, hit counts, token distributions, and request sequences (2 weeks).
Phase 1: Hit-model v1 + simulator - lightweight estimator using exponential decay + prefix recency to forecast hit-rate under TTL changes. Validate with shadow replays (1 week).
Phase 2: Suggestion engine - generate candidate key-tiling (coarser/finer) and TTL ladder proposals with cost/hitrate delta estimates; vet via offline simulator (1 week).
Phase 3: Safe-apply harness - implement canary, steady-state monitor, rollback triggers (SLO breaches, hit drop, error deltas), and policy config UI/API (2 weeks).
Phase 4: Small customer pilots and rollout - run on non-critical tenants, measure economics, iterate on heuristics, then promote to broader fleet (2-4 weeks).
telemetry: Required metrics: per-prefix QPS, cache lookups, misses, miss-token distribution, end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99), error rates, and request sample traces.
Derived signals: estimated marginal hit-rate change when increasing/decreasing TTL, cost-per-token delta, and latency sensitivity distribution by prefix.

Canary thresholds: >3% absolute drop in hit-rate for canary prefix OR >5% relative increase in p99 latency triggers immediate rollback; sustained 10-minute deviation triggers alert and automated revert.
